Okay, I wanted to hold off on making this post until I was done with the replay. I'm kind of mid-way into the winter season right now, but I'll just post some interesting tid bits that I've been thinking of so far lore wise:

We know that the third god calls themselves Pareidolia. If anyone has looked up the term, it is:
"Pareidolia (/ˌpærɪˈdoʊliə, ˌpɛər-/) ; is the tendency for perception to impose a meaningful interpretation on a nebulous stimulus, usually visual, so that one sees an object, pattern, or meaning where there is none. "

The wiki page for this term is of particular interest, as this is the representative picture of the term:



The wiki page goes on to state:
"Common examples are perceived images of animals, faces, or objects in cloud formations, seeing faces in inanimate objects, or lunar pareidolia like the Man in the Moon or the Moon rabbit. The concept of pareidolia may extend to include hidden messages in recorded music played in reverse or at higher- or lower-than-normal speeds, and hearing voices (mainly indistinct) or music in random noise, such as that produced by air conditioners or fans."

"Pareidolia is frequent among patients with Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Pareidolia correlates with age but not autism traits. "

I recommend reading the full wiki page as it could have other interesting tidbits that might link into our story that I've missed.
However, dementia with Lewy bodies is quite interesting in our case:

"Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a type of dementia characterized by changes in sleep, behavior, cognition, movement, and regulation of automatic bodily functions. Memory loss is not always an early symptom."

"REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)—in which people lose the muscle paralysis (atonia) that normally occurs during REM sleep and act out their dreams—is a core feature. RBD may appear years or decades before other symptoms. Other core features are visual hallucinations, marked fluctuations in attention or alertness, and parkinsonism (slowness of movement, trouble walking, or rigidity)."

Of course, I'm not saying this is 100% what Sensei's condition might be, there's a lot of symptoms that obviously don't line up, but a lot of the stuff in those 2 articles does line up.
E.g. Sensei seeing hallucinations of birds, worms, spiders etcetera, or in many happy events there is mention of not being able to move his legs/limbs and so on.

A lot of this game is worded vaguely but what seems to line up to me the most is the most direct answers that the game tells us multiple times; a key event is Baby Finches. What I think this event represents is Sensei, in a dream of sorts, remembering the event of his suicide, so it's kind of a reflection of a memory in a dream so not all the lines said in there or events are meant to be taken at face value. At some point, Maya says his episodes have started since the first loop, but I think they actually started some time after the accident, either caused by DLB or trauma inflicted from losing his family (sidenote: and possibly other stuff as well; as a side note, there's some implications in lines throughout the game that Maya had to bury a child or had a miscarriage or something and this could be a possible trauma source for Sensei as well if it was his).

Baby Finches seems to be an event from before the time loops began, and I think it's a memory of Sensei calling Maya as he is hallucinating at the moment:




What I think Sensei is saying here is: "I just wanted to let you know that I think I might be hallucinating right now." Maya reacts with confusion, to which Sensei clarifies:
"I was just wandering through the [... could be School, could be whatever, not that important] when I saw [I think probably Sekai] and I thought ....[undiscernible, possibly unimportant information].

This is apparently already an established pattern; Maya also doesn't take it that seriously as she says he could have just texted her about it afterwards.



Maya also is revealed to know about the 2nd god in this event, though as always, how much of this is hallucination and how much is fact is vague. I think she later even denies knowing anything about the 2nd god, which personally I think is a lie. There is talk about baby finches and how they'd both be horrible parents, likely because of their each respective abuse traumas. There's more likely hallucination stuff, the event loops back to itself, bla bla, and then Sensei, in a bout of hallucination, jumps off the school roof (which is likely also why the resets happen there).


So, to summarize: in my opinion, Sensei had already in the original life or whatever you want to call it, hallucinations. In a bout of hallucinations, he jumps off the school roof.
It's heavily implied in many events that Maya ressurects him, having extensive theological knowledge, by making a wish from the "wishing well".


The exact wish made is unknown, and seems to have many different parts to it; not simply resurrecting, but creating a "perfect world for Sensei", maybe some variation of "happily ever after". It's clearly a wish from a monkey's paw scenario though, as it seems the gods want something in return; either that Maya cannot get close to Sensei without "breaking" him, or possibly even that "amiokay" is the original iteration of Maya, stuck down in the Wishing Well as part of the deal with the god(s). It is implied multiple times that the various iterations of Sensei until this one were other people controlling his body, but if you look at the character growth he's gotten, I think it's just as likely that they all were him, just not gaining original memories back as quickly, and with more influence from the 1st god (the god of horny). As such his negative qualities of being a lecherous pervert were probably more emphasised and he might've "broken" more easily. In this current iteration, especially after the 1st 2 resets, HOPE mentions that he has to "go somewhere" and that we "probably won't see him for a long time"; it's possible that he has waned somewhat in power and that the 2nd god has increased his power, resulting in Sensei slowly gaining more of his memories, and moving away from the "negative" aspects of the 1st god influencing him into other aspects.

It's interesting to split up the 1 god again and to note the various character traits of the 3 gods; the "callous", the "calm" and the "concerned".
The first god, HOPE, the callous one, seems to want Sensei to "offer up his loved ones" to him; he is likely the one influencing his actions into sexual ones in various ways.
The 2nd god, the wire god, is represented as "calm"; he does not seem to directly speak to the player, and seems most interested in simply allowing things to take their course.
The 3rd god, the "concerned one", we don't know much about, but it seems to want to help and is "concerned" about people.
It's interesting to me that all 3 of these gods represent different character aspects of Sensei himself, ones he already has;
he has a strong libido, he is calm and most likely to allow things to run their course without directly influencing them when he can, and he is also concerned and wants to help people at times. Much like the hallucinations themselves, these are already defining character traits that Sensei has, even though it is implied that the gods influence his actions in given events.
This might mean that the gods are a manifestation of Sensei's character itself, although, this raises a direct conflict with the idea that Sensei was indeed resurrected by "actual" god(s).
So, I don't know what to fully make of it yet, but maybe finishing the replay will give me more ideas. I hope this post was understandable as I can get a bit hectic and not get my point across in long posts like this.

At the end of day it matters little who's eye is that if we don't even know what Nao-chan can or will do, but I guess I just have a hunch that Ami may not be as involved in the matter.

"Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a type of dementia characterized by changes in sleep, behavior, cognition, movement, and regulation of automatic bodily functions. Memory loss is not always an early symptom."

Other core features are visual hallucinations, marked fluctuations in attention or alertness, and parkinsonism (slowness of movement, trouble walking, or rigidity)."

Of course, I'm not saying this is 100% what Sensei's condition might be, there's a lot of symptoms that obviously don't line up, but a lot of the stuff in those 2 articles does line up.
E.g. Sensei seeing hallucinations of birds, worms, spiders etcetera, or in many happy events there is mention of not being able to move his legs/limbs and so on.

A lot of this game is worded vaguely but what seems to line up to me the most is the most direct answers that the game tells us multiple times; a key event is Baby Finches. What I think this event represents is Sensei, in a dream of sorts, remembering the event of his suicide, so it's kind of a reflection of a memory in a dream so not all the lines said in there or events are meant to be taken at face value. At some point, Maya says his episodes have started since the first loop, but I think they actually started some time after the accident, either caused by DLB or trauma inflicted from losing his family (sidenote: and possibly other stuff as well; as a side note, there's some implications in lines throughout the game that Maya had to bury a child or had a miscarriage or something and this could be a possible trauma source for Sensei as well if it was his).

View attachment 2804074

View attachment 2804077

View attachment 2804084

View attachment 2804101

I think she later even denies knowing anything about the 2nd god, which personally I think is a lie. There is talk about baby finches and how they'd both be horrible parents, likely because of their each respective abuse traumas. View attachment 2804130

It's heavily implied in many events that Maya ressurects him, having extensive theological knowledge, by making a wish from the "wishing well".
View attachment 2804148

The exact wish made is unknown, and seems to have many different parts to it; not simply resurrecting, but creating a "perfect world for Sensei", maybe some variation of "happily ever after". It's clearly a wish from a monkey's paw scenario though, as it seems the gods want something in return; either that Maya cannot get close to Sensei without "breaking" him, or possibly even that "amiokay" is the original iteration of Maya, stuck down in the Wishing Well as part of the deal with the god(s). "amiokay" could also just be a representation of Maya's built up anguish over the situation of going through thousands of time loops without being able to get close to her loved one (and watching him do all kinds of deplorable stuff). Also, the parts about this "not being a game" don't mean that it's not a simulation of sorts, made possible by the 2nd god's powers. It's important to remember that the gods are as much 1 entity as they are 3 or 4, and that the 2nd god and the 1st one are still in the end one god that make this wish possible.

It is implied multiple times that the various iterations of Sensei until this one were other people controlling his body, but if you look at the character growth he's gotten, I think it's just as likely that they all were him, just not gaining original memories back as quickly, and with more influence from the 1st god (the god of horny). As such his negative qualities of being a lecherous pervert were probably more emphasised and he might've "broken" more easily. In this current iteration, especially after the 1st 2 resets, HOPE mentions that he has to "go somewhere" and that we "probably won't see him for a long time"; it's possible that he has waned somewhat in power and that the 2nd god has increased his power, resulting in Sensei slowly gaining more of his memories, and moving away from the "negative" aspects of the 1st god influencing him into other aspects.

It's interesting to split up the 1 god again and to note the various character traits of the 3 gods; the "callous", the "calm" and the "concerned".
The first god, HOPE, the callous one, seems to want Sensei to "offer up his loved ones" to him; he is likely the one influencing his actions into sexual ones in various ways.
The 2nd god, the wire god, is represented as "calm"; he does not seem to directly speak to the player, and seems most interested in simply allowing things to take their course.
The 3rd god, the "concerned one", we don't know much about, but it seems to want to help and is "concerned" about people.
It's interesting to me that all 3 of these gods represent different character aspects of Sensei himself, ones he already has;
he has a strong libido, he is calm and most likely to allow things to run their course without directly influencing them when he can, and he is also concerned and wants to help people at times. Much like the hallucinations themselves, these are already defining character traits that Sensei has, even though it is implied that the gods influence his actions in given events.
This might mean that the gods are a manifestation of Sensei's character itself, although, this raises a direct conflict with the idea that Sensei was indeed resurrected by "actual" god(s).
So, I don't know what to fully make of it yet, but maybe finishing the replay will give me more ideas. I hope this post was understandable as I can get a bit hectic and not get my point across in long posts like this.

saerav said:
Okay, I wanted to hold off on making this post until I was done with the replay. I'm kind of mid-way into the winter season right now, but I'll just post some interesting tid bits that I've been thinking of so far lore wise:

We know that the third god calls themselves Pareidolia. If anyone has looked up the term, it is:
"Pareidolia (/ˌpærɪˈdoʊliə, ˌpɛər-/) ; is the tendency for perception to impose a meaningful interpretation on a nebulous stimulus, usually visual, so that one sees an object, pattern, or meaning where there is none. "

The wiki page for this term is of particular interest, as this is the representative picture of the term:

View attachment 2804043

The wiki page goes on to state:
"Common examples are perceived images of animals, faces, or objects in cloud formations, seeing faces in inanimate objects, or lunar pareidolia like the Man in the Moon or the Moon rabbit. The concept of pareidolia may extend to include hidden messages in recorded music played in reverse or at higher- or lower-than-normal speeds, and hearing voices (mainly indistinct) or music in random noise, such as that produced by air conditioners or fans."

"Pareidolia is frequent among patients with Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Pareidolia correlates with age but not autism traits. "

I recommend reading the full wiki page as it could have other interesting tidbits that might link into our story that I've missed.
However, dementia with Lewy bodies is quite interesting in our case:

"Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a type of dementia characterized by changes in sleep, behavior, cognition, movement, and regulation of automatic bodily functions. Memory loss is not always an early symptom."

"REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)—in which people lose the muscle paralysis (atonia) that normally occurs during REM sleep and act out their dreams—is a core feature. RBD may appear years or decades before other symptoms. Other core features are visual hallucinations, marked fluctuations in attention or alertness, and parkinsonism (slowness of movement, trouble walking, or rigidity)."

Of course, I'm not saying this is 100% what Sensei's condition might be, there's a lot of symptoms that obviously don't line up, but a lot of the stuff in those 2 articles does line up.
E.g. Sensei seeing hallucinations of birds, worms, spiders etcetera, or in many happy events there is mention of not being able to move his legs/limbs and so on.

A lot of this game is worded vaguely but what seems to line up to me the most is the most direct answers that the game tells us multiple times; a key event is Baby Finches. What I think this event represents is Sensei, in a dream of sorts, remembering the event of his suicide, so it's kind of a reflection of a memory in a dream so not all the lines said in there or events are meant to be taken at face value. At some point, Maya says his episodes have started since the first loop, but I think they actually started some time after the accident, either caused by DLB or trauma inflicted from losing his family (sidenote: and possibly other stuff as well; as a side note, there's some implications in lines throughout the game that Maya had to bury a child or had a miscarriage or something and this could be a possible trauma source for Sensei as well if it was his).

Baby Finches seems to be an event from before the time loops began, and I think it's a memory of Sensei calling Maya as he is hallucinating at the moment:

View attachment 2804074

View attachment 2804077
What I think Sensei is saying here is: "I just wanted to let you know that I think I might be hallucinating right now." Maya reacts with confusion, to which Sensei clarifies:
"I was just wandering through the [... could be School, could be whatever, not that important] when I saw [I think probably Sekai] and I thought ....[undiscernible, possibly unimportant information].
View attachment 2804084
This is apparently already an established pattern; Maya also doesn't take it that seriously as she says he could have just texted her about it afterwards.

View attachment 2804101

Maya also is revealed to know about the 2nd god in this event, though as always, how much of this is hallucination and how much is fact is vague. I think she later even denies knowing anything about the 2nd god, which personally I think is a lie. There is talk about baby finches and how they'd both be horrible parents, likely because of their each respective abuse traumas. There's more likely hallucination stuff, the event loops back to itself, bla bla, and then Sensei, in a bout of hallucination, jumps off the school roof (which is likely also why the resets happen there).
View attachment 2804130

So, to summarize: in my opinion, Sensei had already in the original life or whatever you want to call it, hallucinations. In a bout of hallucinations, he jumps off the school roof.
It's heavily implied in many events that Maya ressurects him, having extensive theological knowledge, by making a wish from the "wishing well".
View attachment 2804148

The exact wish made is unknown, and seems to have many different parts to it; not simply resurrecting, but creating a "perfect world for Sensei", maybe some variation of "happily ever after". It's clearly a wish from a monkey's paw scenario though, as it seems the gods want something in return; either that Maya cannot get close to Sensei without "breaking" him, or possibly even that "amiokay" is the original iteration of Maya, stuck down in the Wishing Well as part of the deal with the god(s). "amiokay" could also just be a representation of Maya's built up anguish over the situation of going through thousands of time loops without being able to get close to her loved one (and watching him do all kinds of deplorable stuff). Also, the parts about this "not being a game" don't mean that it's not a simulation of sorts, made possible by the 2nd god's powers. It's important to remember that the gods are as much 1 entity as they are 3 or 4, and that the 2nd god and the 1st one are still in the end one god that make this wish possible.

It is implied multiple times that the various iterations of Sensei until this one were other people controlling his body, but if you look at the character growth he's gotten, I think it's just as likely that they all were him, just not gaining original memories back as quickly, and with more influence from the 1st god (the god of horny). As such his negative qualities of being a lecherous pervert were probably more emphasised and he might've "broken" more easily. In this current iteration, especially after the 1st 2 resets, HOPE mentions that he has to "go somewhere" and that we "probably won't see him for a long time"; it's possible that he has waned somewhat in power and that the 2nd god has increased his power, resulting in Sensei slowly gaining more of his memories, and moving away from the "negative" aspects of the 1st god influencing him into other aspects.

It's interesting to split up the 1 god again and to note the various character traits of the 3 gods; the "callous", the "calm" and the "concerned".
The first god, HOPE, the callous one, seems to want Sensei to "offer up his loved ones" to him; he is likely the one influencing his actions into sexual ones in various ways.
The 2nd god, the wire god, is represented as "calm"; he does not seem to directly speak to the player, and seems most interested in simply allowing things to take their course.
The 3rd god, the "concerned one", we don't know much about, but it seems to want to help and is "concerned" about people.
It's interesting to me that all 3 of these gods represent different character aspects of Sensei himself, ones he already has;
he has a strong libido, he is calm and most likely to allow things to run their course without directly influencing them when he can, and he is also concerned and wants to help people at times. Much like the hallucinations themselves, these are already defining character traits that Sensei has, even though it is implied that the gods influence his actions in given events.
This might mean that the gods are a manifestation of Sensei's character itself, although, this raises a direct conflict with the idea that Sensei was indeed resurrected by "actual" god(s).
So, I don't know what to fully make of it yet, but maybe finishing the replay will give me more ideas. I hope this post was understandable as I can get a bit hectic and not get my point across in long posts like this.

I can see it being a plot of a movie which results in you crying at the end or something
